text:
Noah Laba is the Rangers' fourth-line center, a fourth-round pick from Colorado College, and the headlines lately have been blunt: The Hockey Writers and Forever Blueshirts both say the Rangers need more from him. He has five assists and no goals in 18 games.

The numbers back the concern. The Rangers have been about 16 points of expected goal share worse with him on the ice than off it, the biggest gap on the team, at 40% with him out there. His own chances are modest, 1.5 expected goals, so this isn't a finishing problem as much as a shift problem.

What he brings is speed, faster than 92% of the league by NHL Edge, and the penalty kill: Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming shorthanded. That's a real role. Our range has him at 4 to 12 goals over a full season. With the Rangers playing well lately, his line is the one Mike Sullivan will want to stabilize. A first goal would help, but what matters more is getting through shifts without the ice tilting the wrong way.
headline: The Rangers need more from Laba
